facts.fact: Leadership reports the NDPC, with National Commissioner and CEO Dr Vincent Olatunji and a Head of Legal, Enforcement and Regulations, issued a statement and directive in July 2026 after the Federal High Court upheld its power to designate and register Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance; article dated 29 July 2026.

In Emmanuel Harunna v. NDPC (FHC/L/CS/1116/2024) the Federal High Court (Justice F.N. Ogazi) treated the Act as operative law, citing its Section 63 as prevailing over inconsistent law on processing of personal data; the article is dated 29 July 2026 and gives no judgment date.

The court held the NDPC acted within its powers in issuing a Guidance Notice on Registration designating entities in the Major Data Processing - Ordinary High Level category as Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance; the article gives no issue date for the notice and is itself dated 29 July 2026.

The Federal High Court dismissed a challenge by Emmanuel Harunna seeking a declaration that PoS agents are not Data Controllers or Processors of Major Importance and an injunction against their registration, upholding the NDPC's registration power; the judgment date is not given and the article is dated 29 July 2026.

The NDPC directed all unregistered Data Controllers and Processors of Major Importance to register without delay and warned of legal liability for failure, following the court's ruling; reported 29 July 2026.
